title: Border Officers Check More Phones and Laptops
summary:
U.S. border officers are checking more travelers' phones and laptops than ever, according to numbers obtained by the Canadian news outlet CBC News.

Customs and Border Protection, or CBP, checks people and goods coming into the United States. From October 2025 to June 2026, officers searched 52,080 devices. That is more than 32 percent more than the year before.

Most were basic searches, which officers can do without suspecting anything. About 4,564 were deeper searches, where officers may study or copy what is on a device.

CBP says these searches are very rare and help find illegal material and security threats. Esha Bhandari of the American Civil Liberties Union, a group that works on privacy, says Congress should watch the searches more closely.

CBP did not say where the searches happened. One border expert said many people also traveled for the World Cup this summer.
why_it_matters: Many families travel with phones, so it helps to know the rules about searches and privacy.
